hypotheses.title: no app-level body-parser stage: account/settings routes act on bodies pinned ignores and reject in a different order
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: extend the account probe with text/plain and charset scenarios, record pinned once, replay through NewHTTPHandlerWithOptions as internal/server/accounts_test.go:130 does; record the 413/415 bodies as shape (V8 stack)
hypotheses.counterargument: the pinned frontend always sends application/json (upstream/public/script.js:647-658), and the project models body-parser per route where a fixture measured it (internal/server/sd.go:170-209, worldinfo.go:77-82, characters.go:157-185); this family does not.

hypotheses.title: cors.enabled with a falsy cors.origin loses the Express automatic OPTIONS answer (200 vs 404)
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: add null/false/empty-string cors.origin scenarios to the CORS probe, record pinned, replay OPTIONS /api/sprites/get and assert status/Allow/Content-Type/body
hypotheses.counterargument: the shipped default cors.origin is the string "null" (internal/commandline/options.go:289), so only a hand-edited config reaches it; the Go answer is arguably safer but parity is the contract.

hypotheses.title: settings/save empty-body and failure response semantics differ from pinned (file wiped vs 400; 200 {} vs 500)
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: add emptyBody and writeFailure (fault-injected) scenarios to the settings-save probe; assert status/body and, for empty body, the resulting settings.json bytes
hypotheses.counterargument: no frontend path sends an empty or non-JSON save body; the empty-body case would be a data wipe on pinned, so GoTavern's refusal may deserve an explicit product decision rather than a parity fix.

hypotheses.title: panic-boundary 500 bypasses the pinned compression/responseTime wrapper (identity+Content-Length instead of gzip+chunked)
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: record a pinned 500 for a throwing route with headers only (body shape-classified), compare Content-Encoding/Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding for Accept-Encoding: gzip
hypotheses.counterargument: only reachable through a product bug; the body already differs because the V8 stack is deliberately not reproduced (panic_boundary.go:20-43), and writing the page through the compression writer risks a second-status-line hazard.

hypotheses.title: with CSRF disabled and accounts off, /api/users/login gets a nil session and answers 500 where pinned answers 200
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: NewHTTPHandlerWithOptions{AccountsEnabled:false, DisableCSRF:true} plus a default-user record, POST /api/users/login, record pinned with the same config
hypotheses.counterargument: with accounts off the login page redirects to / (internal/server/accounts.go:525-529), so no browser path reaches the route; only an API client or extension fetch would.

hypotheses.title: over TLS the session Set-Cookie attribute order differs (secure after httponly on Go, before on pinned)
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: replay the csrf-session probe over httptest.NewTLSServer and against a pinned TLS listener, compare raw Set-Cookie bytes
hypotheses.counterargument: attribute order is not semantically meaningful (RFC 6265) and secure presence matches; only a byte-comparing TLS differential sees it.

hypotheses.title: one global settings-save mutex is held across disk IO and a content lock, serializing saves across users; no caller cancellation
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: same-run 1-user vs 8-user concurrent POST /api/settings/save (E06), record per-save and mutex-wait p50/p95, decide a per-user coordinator only if red
hypotheses.counterargument: pinned serializes the whole event loop instead, so this is not a parity regression; the critical section is one settings.json plus at most one snapshot copy, and a per-user coordinator adds shutdown/ownership surface that must itself be proven.

hypotheses.title: the throttled trailing settings snapshot is lost on shutdown (parity: pinned also exits without flushing)
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: if a product decision requires durability, add a shutdown flush under the same mutex with a test that cancels a server with a pending save; otherwise the parity statement is the contract
hypotheses.counterargument: flushing would diverge from pinned by writing a backup pinned would not have written at that moment.

hypotheses.title: account version hash uses stored JSON bytes where pinned uses JSON.stringify, so a non-JS-encoded record can invalidate a Node-created session on a backend swap
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: table test over record encodings (literal non-ASCII vs \uXXXX escapes) asserting the Go version equals a pinned-captured version for both; if pinned normalises, hash parsed-then-restringified values
hypotheses.counterargument: node-persist's writer uses JSON.stringify, Go's marshalNodeJSON disables HTML escaping, so a real installation's records are already in JS form.

hypotheses.title: whitelist denials and invalid whitelist entries do not print pinned's console lines
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: pinned boot probes capturing stderr/stdout for a blocked connection, a whitelist.txt boot, and an invalid-pattern config; then the same three boots in Go
hypotheses.counterargument: these are console lines gated by logging.minLogLevel and no committed fixture compares startup console output for these paths; if deliberately out of contract, that decision should be recorded because the state is currently silently different.

hypotheses.title: the settings/world metadata memo has the documented same-size same-mtime residual (no change-stamp witness, unlike the account cache)
hypotheses.reproducer: internal/server/settings_cache_test.go:266 (pins the documented behaviour; not a failing reproducer)
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: if a stronger witness is wanted, hash the change stamp as the account cache does, and measure the extra stat cost on the 1100-document workload before adopting
hypotheses.counterargument: no product writer produces a same-size same-mtime replacement, product writes are proven to invalidate (settings_cache_test.go:174-236), and adding the witness costs a stat per file on the page-load path the cache exists to shorten.

hypotheses.title: Windows account-cache no-witness boundary (re-verification of alpha.15 C-14)
hypotheses.reproducer: internal/server/accounts_cache_test.go:174 (skips/asserts the documented stale value on Windows)
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: none proposed; the boundary is measured and recorded
hypotheses.counterargument: both real writers replace atomically; the remaining window needs an external timestamp-preserving restore.

hypotheses.title: /proxy/:url(*) is in the pinned route set but not in the route-domain table
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: assign an owning lane; if implemented, gate the disabled branch (404 + message) and the enabled branch against a controlled peer
hypotheses.counterargument: this audit owns dispatch composition, not provider routes; the Lead should assign it, and an unimplemented route must answer a distinguishable status (AGENTS rule 17).

hypotheses.title: SSO auto-login is unimplemented but declared and warned about
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: none in M0; a later product decision would need its own probe
hypotheses.counterargument: AGENTS rule 18 is satisfied because the config keys produce an explicit warning; recorded so the browser entry points are complete.

questions: A-H1 needs one pinned recording of non-JSON/empty/oversize bodies on the account and settings routes; the 413/415 bodies embed a V8 stack and must be recorded as shape. Who owns that probe and follow-up?
A-H2: is a falsy cors.origin (null/false/empty string) a supported configuration? The answer decides defect vs documented non-configuration.
A-H4: no gate boots a panic route on pinned; a headers-only pinned panic probe is needed before this can be classified.
A-H5: is disableCsrfProtection plus single-user mode a supported combination? Pinned's login route works there; GoTavern's 500 is either a gap or an unrecorded narrowing.
A-H9: a byte-level check of node-persist and Go writer output for escaped records is needed to decide whether any real writer produces a differing version hash.
Ownership of A-H13 (/proxy) and A-H14 (SSO): neither is this lane's implementation scope.

The middleware chain (internal/server/http.go:544-627) has no single dedicated order gate; ordering evidence is per-feature (internal/server/access_log_test.go:212, cache_buster_test.go:212). Lane E should add a table test of the full order.

No test, build, pinned boot or browser ran in this lane (M0 read-only rule); every reproducer is a plan, and every measured figure above is quoted from the source comment that recorded it, not re-measured.
